noPromise: His 2022 campaign made no specific pledge on housing, homelessness, wildfires, public safety or guns; its Meet Alex page lists those as part of his first-year record, not as promises. His ad's line “I will always put our kids first” is too general to score. As of November 2026 his campaign site still carried the 2022 text, and no separate 2028 campaign site was found. The Stances page has his record on other issues.

promises.why: The Republican voter-ID and citizenship measures he voted against failed to reach 60 votes, but his own voting bills, and the John Lewis bill he cosponsors, have not moved past committee.

actions.text: As Ranking Member of the Senate Rules Committee, led a Democratic floor block against the Republicans' SAVE Act and for election-security funding (Apr 2025).
Voted Nay on waiving budget rules for a Lee amendment to require citizenship for voter registration and photo ID to vote. The motion needed 60 votes and failed 50–49.
Voted Nay on cloture to take up S. 5271, a bill to require voters to show photo identification. Cloture needed 60 votes and failed 52–46.
Original cosponsor of the John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act (S. 2523, July 2025). It was referred to the Judiciary Committee and has had no further action.
Introduced the Voter Purge Protection Act (S. 2994, Oct 2025). It was referred to the Rules Committee and has had no further action.
Introduced the Absentee and Mail Voter Protection Act (S. 4369, Apr 2026). It was referred to the Rules Committee and has had no further action.

promises.issue: Cost of living and working families
promises.promise: I’ll always fight for families working hard to pay the bills.
promises.why: A housing-supply bill he voted for became law, but he was on the losing side of the 2025 reconciliation law, and his own housing bill has not moved. The promise is broad.

actions.text: Voted Nay on the Senate version of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (H.R. 1). It passed 50–50, with the Vice President voting Yea to break the tie.
H.R. 1 became Public Law 119-21 on July 4, 2025.
Called it a “billionaire-first budget reconciliation bill” in his statement after Senate passage (Jul 2025).
Voted Yea on the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (H.R. 6644), a bill to increase the housing supply. It passed the Senate 89–10.
The ROAD to Housing Act became Public Law 119-101 in July 2026.
Introduced the Housing for All Act (S. 1477, Apr 2025), his plan for the housing and homelessness crises. It was referred to the Banking Committee and has had no further action.

promises.why: He voted for every attempt found to extend the ACA premium credits and against the 2025 reconciliation law, but the extensions failed and the law passed.

actions.text: Voted Yea on a Shaheen amendment to the February 2025 budget resolution to preserve and extend the Affordable Care Act's premium tax credits. It was rejected 48–52.
Voted Nay on the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (H.R. 1), which his statement said would cut a trillion dollars from Medicaid. It passed 50–50 and became law.
Voted Yea on cloture to take up S. 3385, Democrats' bill to extend the enhanced ACA premium tax credits. Cloture needed 60 votes and failed 51–48.
Joined California health care leaders to criticize Republicans for not extending the credits (Dec 2025).

promises.promise: Alex Padilla is fighting for us on important issues – defending democracy, climate change, Medicare for All, immigration reform, and more.
promises.why: He cosponsors the bill, but it has not moved beyond referral to committee.

actions.text: Original cosponsor of Sen. Sanders' Medicare for All Act (S. 1506), introduced Apr 29, 2025. It was referred to the Finance Committee and has had no further action.
His release on the reintroduction: “Every American deserves access to high quality, affordable health care, regardless of their zip code or tax bracket.”

promises.promise: Alex remains committed to ensuring that immigration reform is achieved.
promises.why: No immigration reform has been enacted. His registry bill has not moved, and the enforcement bill he opposed became law.

actions.text: Introduced S. 2468 (July 2025) to make the immigration registry under section 249 of the Immigration and Nationality Act available to certain long-term residents. It was referred to the Judiciary Committee and has had no further action.
Voted Nay on the Laken Riley Act (S. 5), which requires DHS to take into custody immigrants charged with theft, among other provisions. It passed 64–35.
The Laken Riley Act became Public Law 119-1.
Voted Yea on waiving budget rules for a Durbin amendment to move ICE funds to the timely processing of DACA applications. The motion needed 60 votes and failed 48–51.

promises.why: He voted against all three resolutions revoking California's clean-air waivers, but they passed and at least one became law. The environmental bills of his found here have not advanced.

actions.text: Voted Nay on H.J.Res. 88, disapproving the EPA waiver for California's Advanced Clean Cars II standards. It passed 51–44.
Voted Nay on H.J.Res. 87, disapproving the EPA waiver for California's heavy-duty vehicle and engine emission standards. It passed 51–45.
Voted Nay on H.J.Res. 89, disapproving the EPA waiver for California's low-NOx engine standards. It passed 49–46.
H.J.Res. 87 became Public Law 119-15.
Spoke repeatedly on the Senate floor against the waiver repeals, which Republicans advanced by overruling the Senate Parliamentarian (May 2025).
Introduced bills with Sens. Booker and Reed to permanently protect the Pacific and Atlantic oceans from offshore drilling (Apr 2025).
